description:
`commands::init::tests::test_profiled_init_authenticates_shipped_v1_once_before_any_publication` asserts on the process-global `shipped_v1_conversion_count`. The counter is shared across concurrently scheduled tests, so the assertion observes bumps caused by tests other than the one under test.

Observed during epic c639cfb5 wave 9: the test passes unfiltered and in isolation, and passes under `--test-threads=1` (284/284 for that filter), but fails under `cargo test -p jit --lib profile` because another test in that filtered set increments the counter concurrently. No profile-lifecycle change touches the counter, so the defect is in the test's use of process-global state rather than in the code under test.

A test whose verdict depends on which other tests are scheduled alongside it is not evidence. It also makes a focused `--lib profile` run unusable as a check during profile work, which is when it is most wanted.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The test observes only the conversions its own scenario causes, so its verdict does not depend on which other tests run concurrently.
- [hard] REQ-02: The test passes under a filtered run that includes it alongside other profile tests, without requiring a single-threaded harness.
- [hard] REQ-03: The authentication-once property it exists to prove is still asserted, not weakened or removed.
title: Shipped-v1 conversion counter makes a profiled-init test order-dependent
